attrs.evidence: Matroid components are the classes of "lie on a common circuit" (Oxley §4.1); for the cycle matroid of a loopless graph the circuits are the cycles and the components are the block edge sets; a separator is a union of components (§4.2) and a partition into separators is a direct-sum decomposition. Verified against κₛ on 117,648 binary federations and on 4,096 n-ary federations, zero mismatches on all three equivalences. This unifies the carriers: for binary constraints the incidence graph is the subdivision of the constraint multigraph, so ONE carrier now covers every arity and the two-carrier machinery retires.
attrs.prior_art: Oxley, Matroid Theory §4.1–4.2 (components, separators, direct sums) — a KNOWN TRANSLATION of a standard matroid fact, not a new theorem. Whitney 1932 for blocks.
attrs.statement: κₛ = 0 if and only if every site's incidence-edge set is a separator of the cycle matroid of the incidence graph — equivalently the site colouring is constant on every matroid component, equivalently the matroid is the direct sum of its site restrictions.
